{{nihongo|'''Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine'''|天佐志比古命神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Oki Province]].

'''Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine''' (あまさしひこのみことじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Chibu, Shimane|Q1204968|qid=Q1204968}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ar|منطقة أوكي (شيمانه)|ceb|Oki-gun|es|Distrito de Oki|fr|District d'Oki|hu|Oki körzet|id|Distrik Oki, Shimane|it|Distretto di Oki|ja|隠岐郡|ko|오키군|pl|Powiat Oki|pt|Distrito de Oki|simple|Oki District, Shimane|zh|隱岐郡|qid=Q735735}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}.

=== Overview ===
Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} and is considered one of the seven shrines of Chibu (Chibu Shichiza) {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=124}}.
Within the village it is called {{ruby|Ichinomiya Shrine|いちのみやじんじゃ}} or “{{ruby|Ichinomiya-san|いっくうさん}}” {{Sfn|Chibu Village Elementary and Junior High School Teachers’ Association|1990|p=100}}.
There is a theater on the shrine grounds where kagura and children’s kabuki are performed {{Sfn|Globe-Trotter Editorial Office|2023|p=37}}.

Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine and Chibu Village Gun District and Chibu Village Elementary and Junior High School 2.jpg|Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine, the Gun district, and {{ill|Chibu Village Elementary and Junior High School|ja|知夫村立知夫小中学校|qid=Q109363695|lt=Chibu Elementary and Junior High School}}

=== Enshrined deity ===
; {{ruby|Amasashihikonomikoto|あまさしひこのみこと}}{{Sfn|Chibu Village Elementary and Junior High School Teachers’ Association|1990|p=100}}
: The deity’s name means a male god who protects a bay—“the place where the sea (ama) cuts in” {{sfn|Toshinoya|1987|p=22}}. He is also known as {{ruby|{{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q276944}}|おおなむちのみこと}} or {{ruby|Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto|おおくにぬしのみこと}}, and is considered the same deity under different names {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=124}}.

It then remained enshrined in the Niburi area for over 1,000 years {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=124}}.

The earliest documentary appearance is in the *{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}*, which records that in the 15th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} (February 848), the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade {{sfn|Takahashi et al.|1996|p=474}}. The *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}* lists it as the minor shrine “Amasashihiko Shrine” {{sfn|Takahashi et al.|1996|p=474}}, and the *{{ill|Izumi Province Divine Name Register|ja|国内神名帳|qid=Q11420490|lt=Oki Province Jinmyōchō}}* records it as “Senior First Rank Amasajihiko Daimyōjin” {{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=951}}{{efn|However, the “Senior First Rank” in the *Oki Province Jinmyōchō* is thought to have been manipulated by the {{ill|Oki clan|ja|億岐氏|qid=Q11387649|lt=Oki no Kuni no Miyatsuko}}, rather than being a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sōgen Senji}} issued by the {{ill|Yoshida family|fr|Clan Yoshida|ja|吉田家|ko|요시다가|simple|Yoshida family|qid=Q11413722}} {{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=951}}.}}. When {{ill|Emperor Go-Daigo|azb|قودایقو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Go-Daigo|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر گۆ-دایگۆ|cs|Go-Daigo|de|Go-Daigo|el|Αυτοκράτορας Γκο-Ντάιγκο|es|Go-Daigo Tennō|fa|امپراتور گودایگو|fi|Go-Daigo|fr|Go-Daigo|hak|Go-Daigo Thiên-fòng|hu|Go-Daigo japán császár|id|Kaisar Go-Daigo|it|Go-Daigo|ja|後醍醐天皇|jv|Kaisar Go-Daigo|ko|고다이고 천황|mr|गो-दाइगो|ms|Maharaja Go-Daigo|nl|Go-Daigo|pl|Go-Daigo|pt|Go-Daigo|ro|Împăratul Go-Daigo|ru|Император Го-Дайго|simple|Emperor Go-Daigo|sr|Го-Даиго|sv|Go-Daigo|sw|Go-Daigo wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิโกไดโงะ|tl|Emperador Go-Daigo|tr|Go-Daigo|uk|Імператор Ґо-Дайґо|vi|Thiên hoàng Go-Daigo|wuu|后醍醐天皇|yo|Emperor Go-Daigo|zh|後醍醐天皇|zh_classical|後醍醐天皇|zh_min_nan|Go-Daigo Thian-hông|zh_yue|後醍醐天皇|qid=Q313942}} was exiled to Oki in {{ill|1332|Q6001|qid=Q6001}}, he visited Chibu Village and worshiped at Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=124}}.

=== Early modern period ===
[[File:Ikku-jinja kyushachi niburi.jpg|thumb|Former shrine site in Niburi]]
In the *Shimazen Muramura Jinmyōki* of the 16th year of {{ill|Genroku|ar|فترة غنروكو|cs|Genroku|de|Genroku|es|Genroku|fa|گنروکو|fr|Ère Genroku|id|Genroku|it|Genroku|ja|元禄|ko|겐로쿠|pt|Genroku|ru|Гэнроку|simple|Genroku|sk|Genroku|sr|Генроку|sv|Genroku|tr|Genroku|zh|元祿|qid=Q1325001}} ({{ill|1703|Q6822|qid=Q6822}}), the shrine is referred to as “Amasashihiko-no-Mikoto Shrine <small>alias Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, Ichinomiya Daimyōjin of Chibu Village</small>,” indicating that it came to be called “Ichinomiya” in the early modern period, meaning “the ichinomiya of Chibu Village” {{sfn|Takahashi et al.|1996|p=474}}{{efn|At this time, only the *Shimazen Muramura Jinmyōki* explicitly identifies Ichinomiya Shrine with the “Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine” of the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō* {{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=952}}. The *Jinja Kakuroku* states “Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine (omitted) location unknown” {{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=952}}. Toward the end of the Edo period, multiple works such as the *Inshū Kokishū* and the *Shingi-shi* section of the *{{ill|Dai Nihonshi|Q1156003|qid=Q1156003}}* began to identify Ichinomiya Shrine with Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine {{sfn|Matsuura|1983|p=952}}.}}.

In the 2nd year of {{ill|Manji (era)|Q1145295|qid=Q1145295}} ({{ill|1659|Q6995|qid=Q6995}}), the shrine was moved from the Niburi (Niifuri) area to its current location in the Gun area {{sfn|Takahashi et al.|1996|p=474}}{{efn|A ridge tag also bears the inscription “Auspicious day, October, Manji 2 (Kinoe-I)” {{sfn|Takahashi et al.|1996|p=474}}.}}.

During the {{ill|Meiwa|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161}} era, following the stranding of a whale, children began dedicating hand dances {{Sfn|San’in no Kamigami Publishing Association|2011|p=69}}. From around the {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} era these dances evolved into forms closer to {{ill|Kabuki|Q199701|qid=Q199701}} <ref>{{Cite book|ja|author=Shimane Prefectural Board of Education |title=History of Shimane Prefecture |publisher=Hōkōsha |date=1973-3-25 |page=344}}</ref>{{Full|date=July 2024}}{{efn|It is said that during the Bunsei era, a man named Ryōsaku from Tasawa in Chibu Village choreographed and taught theatrical dances {{sfn|Takahashi et al.|1996|p=474}}.}} and by 1998 had become close to the current form of village theater {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=125}}.

=== Modern period ===
{{Questionable|The year {{ill|1969|Q11185774|qid=Q11185774}} (Shōwa 39)|date=2024-07}} A reconstruction {{ill|Sengū|Q2271023|qid=Q2271023}} festival was held {{Sfn|Chibu Village History Compilation Committee|1996|p=851}}.

=== Shrine grounds ===
; Stone where Emperor Go-Daigo sat
: A stone said to be where {{ill|Emperor Go-Daigo|azb|قودایقو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Go-Daigo|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر گۆ-دایگۆ|cs|Go-Daigo|de|Go-Daigo|el|Αυτοκράτορας Γκο-Ντάιγκο|es|Go-Daigo Tennō|fa|امپراتور گودایگو|fi|Go-Daigo|fr|Go-Daigo|hak|Go-Daigo Thiên-fòng|hu|Go-Daigo japán császár|id|Kaisar Go-Daigo|it|Go-Daigo|ja|後醍醐天皇|jv|Kaisar Go-Daigo|ko|고다이고 천황|mr|गो-दाइगो|ms|Maharaja Go-Daigo|nl|Go-Daigo|pl|Go-Daigo|pt|Go-Daigo|ro|Împăratul Go-Daigo|ru|Император Го-Дайго|simple|Emperor Go-Daigo|sr|Го-Даиго|sv|Go-Daigo|sw|Go-Daigo wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิโกไดโงะ|tl|Emperador Go-Daigo|tr|Go-Daigo|uk|Імператор Ґо-Дайґо|vi|Thiên hoàng Go-Daigo|wuu|后醍醐天皇|yo|Emperor Go-Daigo|zh|後醍醐天皇|zh_classical|後醍醐天皇|zh_min_nan|Go-Daigo Thian-hông|zh_yue|後醍醐天皇|qid=Q313942}}, exiled to {{ill|Oki Province|Q1063829|qid=Q1063829|lt=Oki}} in the 2nd year of {{ill|Genkō (1331–1334)|Q1194556|qid=Q1194556}} ({{ill|1332|Q3844595|qid=Q3844595}}), sat to rest when he worshiped at Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine {{Sfn|Chibu Village History Compilation Committee|1996|p=851}}.
; Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine Theater
: A {{ill|Rural Kabuki Stage|Q22124550|qid=Q22124550}} with a {{ill|Revolving stage|Q253227|qid=Q253227}}, featuring stone embankment-style seating at the front; designated a village cultural property <ref name="Cultural Properties List">{{Cite web |ja |url=http://www.vill.chibu.lg.jp/gyosei/about/9 |title=List of Cultural Properties |publisher=Chibu Village |accessdate=2024-06-29}}</ref>. Community festivals such as Minai Odori are held here {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=124}}.
; Tōshō Daigongen
: Origins unknown {{Sfn|Chibu Village History Compilation Committee|1996|p=852}}.
; Wrestlers’ monument
: Bears the inscription “Meiji 15: Tatsunami Yashichi, Wakagumi, Manriki Yonekichi, Chūren,” with the names of two wrestlers {{Sfn|Chibu Village History Compilation Committee|1996|p=856}}. Both were {{ill|Rikishi|Q2727289|qid=Q2727289}} from the Gun district, commemorated for their great success {{Sfn|Chibu Village History Compilation Committee|1996|p=856}}.
; Ebisu-san
: An {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|Q1129330|qid=Q1129330}} statue with the inscription “2nd year of {{ill|Kaei|Q1146125|qid=Q1146125}}, Kaizen of Shōyō-ji” {{Sfn|Chibu Village History Compilation Committee|1996|p=855}}.
; Seishin Sakō Monument
: Inscribed with “Do you not know the prowess of Japanese soldiers? Governor of Shimane Prefecture {{ill|Masaki Fukumura|Q11594448|qid=Q11594448}}” {{Sfn|Chibu Village History Compilation Committee|1996|p=859}}. It commemorates Sugiyama Yasuichi from the Ōe district, who was killed in action in the 7th year of {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}; even after being wounded by a spear, he continued fighting while loudly proclaiming the words on the monument, leading to its erection in praise of his spirit {{Sfn|Chibu Village History Compilation Committee|1996|p=859}}.

=== Events ===
[[File:Ichinomiya Shrine Grand Festival.jpg|thumb|Ichinomiya Shrine Grand Festival]]

; Minai Odori
: A dance dedicated on the 15th day of the 8th month of the lunar calendar to pray for a good harvest {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=128}}. It is performed to the singing of “Hā—everyone line up together, let us show you the dancers’ movements, sā-sasasa” {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=128}}. Designated an intangible cultural property of the village <ref name="Shrine Map" />.
; Ichinomiya Shrine Grand Festival
: Held every two years (even-numbered years) in late July {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=124}}. Theatrical offerings are presented {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=124}}. Performances such as {{ill|Sanbasō|Q11356796|qid=Q11356796}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiranami Gonin Otoko}} are staged by junior high school students {{Sfn|Oki History and Folklore Research Association|1998|p=124}}. The origin of the performances dates to the {{ill|Meiwa|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161}} era of the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, when after a whale stranding and a subsequent epidemic in the village, children’s hand dances were dedicated {{Sfn|San’in no Kamigami Publishing Association|2011|p=69}}.
; Ten-sha pilgrimage
: In Chibu there is a custom called the Ten-sha pilgrimage, in which people visit ten shrines in the village to pray for the success of surgery or to mark the end of mourning after a death {{Sfn|Chibu Village History Compilation Committee|1996|p=765}}. Amasashihikonomikoto Shrine is one of these ten shrines {{Sfn|Yama|2020|p=43}}{{Sfn|Chibu Village History Compilation Committee|1996|p=766}}.

=== Village-designated cultural properties ===
; Tangible cultural property
: Amasashihiko Shrine Theater – designated April 1, 1995 (Heisei 7) <ref name="Cultural Properties List" />{{efn|Prior to this, the theater had been designated a “tangible cultural property” by the Shimane Dōzen Board of Education in 1973 (Shōwa 48) {{sfn|Takahashi et al.|1996|p=474}}.}}.
; Intangible folk cultural property
: Minai Odori – designated November 1, 2001 (Heisei 13) <ref name="Cultural Properties List" />.
